episode.title: What If Napoleon Marched Into Genghis Khan?
episode.notes: P0c agent A/B test, arm B, stage 1 (story-architect): story layer only; 8 segments, about 5 minutes, template A

periods.question: Can the army that wins by one decisive battle read ground that does not offer one?
periods.bottleneck: the column's hunger and the wagons

periods.question: Does a won battle matter against an enemy who never stood to lose it?
What does the road home cost, and who can say it?
periods.bottleneck: the word carried between two men with no shared tongue

napoleon.card: Napoleon Bonaparte as our caricature: short stocky man, grey greatcoat over a green coat, black bicorne hat worn sideways, one hand tucked in his waistcoat, a spyglass

speech.style: Clipped and commanding: short declarative orders, military maxims, no small talk, impatient with questions; toward the khan he sizes him up like a rival marshal, toward Ali he uses him as a tool and never asks his name; never admits the army is already beaten by hunger.
sources: manner as generally described (terse, offensive-minded, C04); to be checked by the creator, not independently fetched

genghis.card: Genghis Khan as our caricature: broad weathered man, thin braided grey beard, fur-trimmed felt cap, brown leather lamellar coat, a horsehair standard behind him, a short composite bow

speech.style: Slow, plain and concrete: short sentences built from horses, grass, herds and a man's word; asks questions instead of boasting; toward Napoleon he is a host listening to a guest who talks of himself, toward Ali the first man in the room worth asking; never admits he is impressed by the long guns.
sources: manner as generally described (promotes by merit and loyalty, C11); to be checked by the creator, not independently fetched

ali.card: Ali, a young Mameluke rider of the Guard: lean, watchful, red turban with a white plume, wide yellow trousers, a curved sabre, a Crimean Tatar by birth

speech.style: Quick, dry and careful: short sentences, watches mouths before he speaks, says 'Sire' with a tired edge; toward Napoleon loyal but tired of being only a mouth, toward the khan the first listener who hears tone; never admits he is afraid or that he softens words to stay alive.

drama.premise: In 1812 a column of Napoleon's army walks out of a fog into the steppe of 1223, where Genghis Khan will not stand still to be destroyed and the only bridge between them is a Mameluke interpreter.
drama.question: Can Napoleon get the one decisive battle that has always ended his wars?
drama.promise: the man who needs one great battle meets the man who never offers one: the guns, the burning wagons and the price of the road home

napoleon.need: to accept a limit and pay for the road home
napoleon.flaw: cannot leave a field unfinished and cannot listen
napoleon.change: gives up his own guns to bring the column out

genghis.want: to learn what the iron guns can do and to own them
genghis.flaw: cannot resist a weapon he does not have

ali.want: to carry words that keep the column alive
ali.flaw: softens the truth to stay safe

loops.question: can Napoleon get the one decisive battle?
who is the rider watching from the far ridge?
how long can the column eat without the road?
what will the khan ask for when they talk?

setups.what: Napoleon the artillery officer and his guns
the khan keeps the archer who admitted shooting his horse
Ali understands a shout in a Kipchak tongue

ending.note: fog and silent drums open and close the film; the guns left on the grass are the payoff of the artillery officer's pride

segments.beat: The fog opens on the 1812 column and the drums go quiet on grass that is 589 years too early.
segments.purpose: NARRATOR only, ~50 words: hook, no dialogue. Plant the promise and the gap (what is out there?). Claims: I01, C21.

lines.text: The drums stop first.

visual_beats.why: the drums that stop first

lines.text: Then the fog lifts, and the whole column stands in grass that belongs to another century.

visual_beats.why: the fog lifts on the column
grass from another century: time is off

lines.text: Not decades off. Five hundred and eighty-nine years early.

visual_beats.why: counts the 589 years early

lines.text: Napoleon came for one great battle. Who out here is going to give it to him?

visual_beats.why: rings Napoleon, who came for the battle
the one great battle he came for
asks who out here will give it

segments.beat: A tired column with food for days meets an enemy who wins by never standing still; the narrator lays out the two ways of war.
segments.purpose: NARRATOR only, ~95 words: orientation and stakes. Napoleon the gunner who wants the decisive battle, the wagons that cannot follow, 3-4 horses per Mongol and the khan who kept the archer who admitted shooting his horse (plants P01, P02). Claims: C01, C02, C04, C08, C11, C16.

drama.stakes: the army eats only what the wagons and the road give it

lines.text: Napoleon crossed the Neman with 450,000 men. Moscow saw about 100,000 of them.

visual_beats.why: counts the 450,000 men who crossed
only about 100,000 reached Moscow

lines.text: He's a gunner at heart. Find the enemy's army, break it in one battle, go home.

visual_beats.why: a gunner at heart means cannon
break the enemy in one battle

lines.text: But his wagons can't follow these tracks, so the column eats what it grabs along the road.

visual_beats.why: the wagons that cannot follow
the wagons can't follow the tracks

lines.text: Out here, nobody grabs anything for free. Every Mongol rider keeps three or four horses and swaps mounts as he goes.

visual_beats.why: three or four horses per rider

lines.text: And Genghis Khan once kept the archer who shot his horse. The man owned up to it.

visual_beats.why: rings the khan who kept the archer
the archer who shot his horse
the man owned up honestly

lines.text: So what does a man who needs one battle do with an enemy who never needs to stand?

visual_beats.why: asks what the gunner does
an enemy who never needs to stand

segments.beat: Napoleon wants Murat's cavalry loosed after riders who run too neatly; Ali, who knows how steppe riders flee, says the runners are leading them on.
segments.purpose: SCENE ~130 words (napoleon, ali), narrator in/out. Skirmish: Murat's blown horses, the feigned retreat, a rider on the far ridge who watches (opens L02), Ali understands a shout in a Kipchak tongue (plants P03). Claims: C10, C13, C14, C15, I03.

drama.stakes: a whole wing of cavalry rides away from the column

lines.text: Murat's riders are chasing a handful of runners, on horses he never bothers to count.

visual_beats.why: the handful of runners being chased

lines.text: On the far ridge, one rider sits still and watches.

visual_beats.why: rings the one rider on the far ridge

lines.text: Napoleon wants the second wave loose before dark, and Ali, his Mameluke interpreter, stands at his stirrup.

visual_beats.why: names Ali, the Mameluke interpreter

lines.text: Murat has them. Send the second wave.
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: the order lands with a set jaw

lines.text: Sire, with respect, they run slowly.
lines.speaker: ali

lines.text: Slow or fast, they run. That is enough.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: The shout from the ridge, Sire. It is near my mother's tongue. It says, come on.
lines.speaker: ali

visual_beats.why: listener's face on the reveal of the shout

lines.text: Everyone shouts in a retreat.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: Look at the dust behind the ridge. They are leading Murat on.
lines.speaker: ali

visual_beats.why: points at the dust behind the ridge
listener's face as the trap is named

lines.text: Then recall him.
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: The trumpets will not carry, Sire. He is over the crest.
lines.speaker: ali

visual_beats.why: the order can no longer be recalled

lines.text: Then the wing follows him. Bring up the guns.
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: the guns he orders brought up

visual_beats.why: counts the nine days of following the retreat

visual_beats.why: the deadline of dark for the wing

scene.place: a low rise of dry grass above the first valley, the column strung out behind
scene.time: midday, an hour after the fog lifted
scene.why_now: Murat's cavalry has just charged a handful of riders and the riders are running
scene.want: to loose the second wave after the runners and finish them before dark
scene.obstacle_want: to stop the pursuit because the runners flee too slowly and too neatly
scene.turn: Ali points at the dust behind the ridge: the runners are drawing Murat on, and the order cannot be recalled in time (asymmetric: emperor and interpreter).
scene.surface_topic: whether to send the second wave
scene.real_subject: whether the Emperor still reads the ground or only his plan

segments.beat: Napoleon turns to what he trusts, the guns and the squares, and the valley battle breaks the first wave; the army believes it has won.
segments.purpose: NARRATOR with a few shouted orders, ~120 words, no played scene. Guns reach 900 m, bows 400 m, muskets only 90 m, squares hold under cavalry. A false victory that makes him lean on the guns. Claims: C05, C06, C07, C09, C20, I03.

drama.stakes: the guns and powder are the army's last strength

lines.text: Napoleon stops guessing and starts measuring. His twelve-pounders reach nine hundred meters.

visual_beats.why: counts the nine hundred meters of gun reach

lines.text: The Mongol bow tops out near four hundred. A French musket, ninety.

visual_beats.why: bars compare four hundred and ninety meters

lines.text: Guns forward! Form squares!
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: the guns ordered forward

lines.text: A steady square holds its fire until the horsemen are close, and cavalry alone rarely breaks one.

visual_beats.why: the steady square that holds its fire

lines.text: Down the valley comes a tumen, ten thousand riders, straight into the guns.

visual_beats.why: rings the ten thousand riders coming down the valley

lines.text: Hold your fire! Wait for them!
lines.speaker: napoleon

lines.text: They never get close. The first wave comes apart under the round shot, and the survivors turn and ride.

visual_beats.why: the riders never get close

lines.text: Fire!
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: the order Fire lands as the blow

lines.text: By afternoon the valley belongs to the army. Men cheer, and the guns stay hot.

visual_beats.why: the army believes the valley is won

lines.text: The Emperor has the battle he marched here for. So he trusts his guns even more.

visual_beats.why: the guns he trusts even more

segments.beat: At dusk the tumens do not return to the field: they ride round the victory and burn the wagons; the rider on the ridge is Genghis Khan.
segments.purpose: NARRATOR ~95 words, the midpoint reversal: the wagons burn, the army can no longer feed itself, the watcher is the khan with about two tumens. Closes L02, L03; opens L04. Claims: C16, C20, I02, I03.

drama.stakes: no wagons means no bread, and the foraging road is now the khan's

lines.text: Dusk. The tumens do not come back to the field.

visual_beats.why: Dusk marks the hour the tumens turn
the tumens do not come back to the field

lines.text: They ride around the victory instead, two tumens, twenty thousand riders, and not one of them stops to fight.

visual_beats.why: counts twenty thousand riders in two tumens

lines.text: Torches go into the wagon canvas. By midnight the bread is smoke.

visual_beats.why: the torches that go into the canvas
the wagon canvas set alight
the bread is smoke, the supply is gone

lines.text: The men who cheered at noon sit watching their supper burn, and the foraging road they live on now belongs to the riders.

visual_beats.why: the supper they watch burn

lines.text: On the far ridge, the rider who watched all day lifts one hand. That's Genghis Khan himself.

visual_beats.why: rings the far ridge where the rider stands
names the watcher as Genghis Khan himself

lines.text: He never needed to win the Emperor's battle. So what does he want, when he finally speaks?

visual_beats.why: he never needed to win the battle
asks what the khan wants

segments.beat: Under a truce sign Napoleon demands his battle at dawn; the khan, who never answers the challenge, asks only how far the long guns shoot.
segments.purpose: SCENE ~135 words (napoleon, genghis, ali), narrator in/out. The parley begins: Napoleon the proud artillery officer tells the range exactly; Moscow's silence from Alexander I stings him because this enemy does talk. Claims: C04, C05, C12, I04.

drama.stakes: the road home and the army's pride

lines.text: A white cloth goes up on a lance at the edge of the burnt wagon line.

visual_beats.why: the white cloth goes up as the truce sign

lines.text: Napoleon rides out with Ali at his stirrup. The khan waits on a felt rug, in no hurry at all.

visual_beats.why: the khan waits on a felt rug

lines.text: Dawn. Open ground. My army against yours.
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: Dawn is the hour he demands

lines.text: He asks for a battle at dawn, Great Khan. On open ground.
lines.speaker: ali

lines.text: The grass is wide. Tell him to sit.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: I do not sit. Repeat my terms.
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: the refusal to sit lands hard

lines.text: He stands, Great Khan. He says the terms are not for sitting.
lines.speaker: ali

visual_beats.why: Ali keeps a straight face softening the words

lines.text: Alexander gave me five weeks of silence. You, at least, came to the table.
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: counts the five weeks of Moscow's silence
listener's face on the reveal that this enemy talks

lines.text: Ask him how far the long guns shoot.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Sire, the khan asks how far the long guns reach.
lines.speaker: ali

lines.text: Nine hundred meters, round shot. Six hundred, canister. Fifteen men to a gun.
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: bars compare nine hundred and six hundred meters
counts fifteen men to a gun
listener's face as the gun's reach is told

lines.text: The night turns cold on the burnt wagon line. By morning, the khan will name his price.

visual_beats.why: asks what price the khan will name

scene.place: the burnt wagon line at dusk, a felt rug on a rise where the khan sits his horse
scene.time: the evening after the wagons burn
scene.why_now: a rider spared by the khan has carried the word that the khan will talk
scene.want: to force a battle at dawn that the guns can win
scene.obstacle_want: to learn what the iron guns can do and what the foreigner will pay for the road home
scene.turn: Genghis ignores the challenge and asks how far the long guns shoot, and Napoleon proudly answers (balanced: two rulers).
scene.real_subject: who is the host and who is the guest on this grass

segments.beat: At dawn the khan names two guns as the price of the road; Ali softens the Emperor's insult, the khan hears the tone, and Ali confesses.
segments.purpose: SCENE ~140 words (napoleon, genghis, ali), narrator in/out. The climax: the price, the softened word, the confession answered by the khan's merit rule (pays P02); Napoleon gives up his guns (pays P01). Claims: C11, C15, I04.

lines.text: Dawn. Napoleon, the khan and Ali stand with two iron guns between them, and the fog at the valley's far end is thinning. When the sun burns it off, the way home closes.

visual_beats.why: the two iron guns between the men
the way home closes at sunrise

lines.text: Tell him my price. The long guns. All of them.
lines.speaker: genghis

visual_beats.why: the listener hears all the guns demanded

lines.text: Sire, the khan asks for the guns. For the road.
lines.speaker: ali

lines.text: Tell this horse thief a gunner gives up his guns when he is dead.
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: the insult leaves his mouth hot

lines.text: He says a gunner is fond of his guns, Great Khan.
lines.speaker: ali

visual_beats.why: a flat face hides the softened word

lines.text: Your voice dropped. Say it again, as he said it.
lines.speaker: genghis

visual_beats.why: the khan has heard the tone

lines.text: Your tongue is near my mother's. I hear what you hear. He called you a horse thief.
lines.speaker: ali

visual_beats.at: He called you a horse thief
visual_beats.why: the khan takes the insult without a flicker

lines.text: I kept an archer who shot my horse and told me so. Tell me true, always.
lines.speaker: genghis

visual_beats.why: the listener's face where the merit rule lands

lines.text: Two guns, not all. Let him choose.
lines.speaker: genghis

lines.text: Take the two on the left. Quickly.
lines.speaker: napoleon

visual_beats.why: a flat face swallows giving up the guns

lines.text: The sun climbs. Two guns will stay on the grass, and the khan's hand is already moving toward the first barrel.

visual_beats.why: counts the price down to two guns

scene.place: the same rise at dawn, two iron guns standing on the grass between the men
scene.time: dawn, the fog thinning at the valley's far end
scene.why_now: the fog that carried them in is thinning and the way home closes at sunrise
scene.want: to carry the words across without either man's pride getting the column killed
scene.obstacle_want: to have every word of the Emperor's demand carried exactly, with the guns kept
scene.turn: Ali softens the Emperor's insult, the khan asks again and Ali admits the change; the khan lowers the price to two guns (indirect: politeness hides the blade).
scene.real_subject: who may be afraid in front of whom

segments.beat: The fog returns, the column walks out without two guns, and the khan's hand rests on a French barrel: no battle ended this war.
segments.purpose: NARRATOR ~70 words, the resolution and bookend: answers L01 (no, he got his battle and it ended nothing), mirrors S01's fog and drums. Claims: C21, C01, I01.

drama.stakes: the road back and the guns left behind

lines.text: Behind them, the khan's hand rests on a French barrel.

visual_beats.why: the khan's hand on a French barrel

lines.text: Now they walk out through a fog, and the steppe is only grass again, 589 years from home.
